newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown seeks fresh debate on single currency.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown seeks fresh debate on single currency.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown try to spark fresh debate on European monetary union will on Thursday by giving a speech and publishing a report on the issue, newspapers said.
They said Brown will also publish separate guides for the public and business next week on the likely implications of European monetary union for Britain.

The Times and The Independent newspapers said that Brown's speech and the report by Lord Currie, a Professor at the London School of Economics, will leave Britain's current stance on monetary union unchanged.
The Labour government, which came to power in May, has said Britain is unlikely to join a single currency at its planned start in 1999.

Nevertheless, Brown will tell the Royal Institute for International Affairs on Thursday that the arguments for and against joining must be openly debated because of the "profound implications" either would have for the economy.
If Britain were to be among the first wave of countries to join the single currency, it would have to give notification this summer.
But the Independent quoted a Treasury official as saying it may be possible to ask for "more latitude" if the government decided later that it wanted to join in 1999.
The government has promised a referendum before the decision to join or stay out is taken.
